comments.author: @wunderbar2058
comments.text:
As an Angolan🇦🇴, I’m glad that my country naturally supplies 95% of water for the Okavango Delta. We have plenty of annual rivers in our backyard.

Okavango Delta is a natural beauty that gives life to wild life in Botswana in particular, boosts tourism etc and highlights the beauty of Africa. 

However, I hope that people from Angola and Namibia DO NOT interfere with this natural water supply by building dams, mining activities along the supplying rivers or any action or lack thereof that would compromise the BIGGEST DELTA in the world. 

We came to this world and found the Delta, let’s preserve it, and leave it intact for future generations.

replies.author: @stewarttau1451
replies.text: Yes. Watching from the Capital City Gabs🦓. Nice documentary, but the narration leaves a lot 2 B desired. Where he spoke about wild dogs, it sounded like he was saying WILDOGS KILL THE OLD ONES AMONG THEMSELVES AND FEED IT TO THE SICK AND THE YOUNG FIRST. The real truth is that after catching prey wilddogs start eating even without killing their victim, tearing away large chunks of meat, which they swallow and store in their bellies. When they return to their den, they regurgitate some of the meat from their stomachs and feed the "baby sitter", the cubs and the elderly. If no cubs, they simply rest at their den and await the next hunting expedition.
